questions.question_english:
An establishment employs 18 direct workers and
25 contract workers. Does the Contract Labour
(Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 apply to
this establishment?
options_english:
No, because the total direct workers are less
than 20.

No, because the overall workforce must
exceed 50 for the Act to apply.

Yes, because the number of contract workers
is 20 or more.

Yes, but only if the direct workers agree to
the application of the Act.
questions.explanation_english:
Yes, because the number of contract workers
is 20 or more.
Section 1(4)(a) specifies that the Act applies
to any establishment employing twenty or
more workmen as contract labour on any day
of the preceding twelve months. The count of
direct employees is irrelevant for determining
applicability; since twenty-five contract workers
are deployed, the numerical threshold is satisfied
and the establishment is fully covered.
questions.explanation_hindi: अधिनियम की प्रयोज्यता सीधे नियुक्त कर्मियों की कुल संख्या पर नहीं, बल्कि ठेका श्रमिकों की निर्धारित सीमा पर निर्भर करती है।

questions.question_english:
Under the definitions provided in the Contract
Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970,
does a person employed mainly in a managerial or
administrative capacity qualify as a “workman”?
options_english:
Yes, provided his monthly salary remains
strictly below the statutory prescribed limit

Yes, he qualifies as a workman regardless of
his salary level or job designation

No, persons in managerial or administrative

questions.explanation_english:

administrative capacity from the statutory
definition of a workman. Consequently, such
individuals cannot be classified as contract labour
under the Act, regardless of their specific wage
levels, contractual arrangements, or assigned
technical job titles within the establishment.

questions.question_english:
A school Principal finds that the security guards
sent by the outsourced agency have changed
without his prior knowledge. Do these new
guards still fall under the definition of ‘contract
labour’ for the school?
options_english:
No, because the Principal employer had no
prior knowledge or formal approval of their
individual hiring.

No, because they did not sign a direct
tripartite employment agreement with the
Principal Employer.

Yes, because contract labour can be hired
with or without the knowledge of the
principal employer.

Yes, but they automatically transition to
become permanent direct employees of the
school administration.
questions.explanation_english:
Yes, because contract labour can be hired
with or without the knowledge of the principal
employer.
Section 2(1)(b) explicitly states that a workman
is deemed contract labour when hired through
a contractor, with or without the knowledge
of the principal employer. Therefore, changing
individual guards without prior approval from
the Head of School does not alter their legal
classification as contract labour under the Act.

with or without the knowledge of the
principal employer.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the fundamental objectives of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970:
I. To abolish contract labour wherever possible and practicable.
II. To ensure that contractors operate without the need for government licensing.
III. To regulate the working conditions of contract labour where abolition is not possible.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english:
I and III only
The fundamental objectives of the Act are to
regulate the employment of contract labour
in establishments where complete abolition
is not feasible and to abolish contract labour
in processes where abolition is practicable.
Contractors are strictly required to obtain
official licenses rather than operating without
oversight, ensuring full regulatory compliance
and statutory worker protection.

questions.question_english:
The Delhi Government decides to abolish
contract labour in the activity of ‘teaching’
in all government schools, determining it to
be a perennial, core activity necessary for the
establishment. According to the Contract Labour
(Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, what is
the correct legal sequence for this abolition?

Government issues order → Consults
Advisory Board → Publishes Notification

Publishes Notification → Approves in

the Advisory Board, evaluating criteria under
Section 10(2) (perennial nature, necessity,
regular workforce practices), and issuing a formal
prohibition notification in the Official Gazette to
complete legal abolition.

questions.question_english:
The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition)
Act, 1970 extends to which geographical
jurisdiction?

The whole of India except the State of

The whole of India

labour laws apply uniformly across all States and
Union Territories, ensuring standardized legal
rights, regulatory mechanisms, and protection for
contract workers nationwide without geographic
distinction.

options_hindi: शिकायत करने वाले कर्मचारियों को तुरंत हटाकर स्थानीय श्रमिकों को दैनिक आधार पर नियुक्त करना
विद्यालय के मुख्य द्वार बंद करके सभी कक्षाएँ निलंबित करना और अवकाश घोषित करना
सामान्य कामकाज बाधित करने के लिए हड़ताली कर्मचारियों के विरुद्ध पुलिस प्राथमिकी दर्ज करना

questions.question_english:
If outsourced sanitation workers go on strike
complaining that the contractor is paying
them less than the minimum wage, what is the
FIRST appropriate administrative action for the
Principal?
options_english:
Immediately terminate the complaining
workers and hire substitute daily wagers
directly from the local labor market.

Lock the main school gates, suspend all
classes, and officially declare an emergency
school holiday for all staff.

File an official Police FIR against the striking
workers for causing public disruption to
normal school functioning.

Verify wage registers and pay unpaid
amounts directly to workers, deducting from
the bill.
questions.explanation_english:
Verify wage registers and pay unpaid
amounts directly to workers, deducting from the
bill.
Section 21(4) dictates that if a contractor fails
to pay statutory minimum wages, the Principal
Employer must pay unpaid amounts directly
to the contract workers and deduct those sums
from the contractor’s pending bills.

amounts directly to workers, deducting from
the bill.

questions.question_english:
When the Principal Employer pays the wages
because the contractor has defaulted, how can
the Principal Employer recover this amount?
options_english:
By filing a civil recovery suit in the
jurisdictional District Court, which usually
takes several years to reach final judgment.

By deducting the amount from money
payable to the contractor under any contract
or debt.

By making a corresponding percentage
deduction from the monthly salaries and
allowances of all regular direct employees.

The Principal Employer is legally barred
from recovering the disbursed amount as
it stands classified as a statutory default
penalty.

By deducting the amount from money

debt.
Section 21(4) dictates that if the contractor fails

them. The Principal Employer can recover the
amount so paid from the contractor by deducting

a debt.

payable to the contractor under any contract

हाँ, क्योंकि कंप्यूटर आपूर्तिकर्ता एजेंसी प्रतिष्ठान के लिए ठोस परिणाम दे रही है

questions.question_english:
An agency supplies computers to a school and
sends two technicians to install them over two
days. Are these technicians “contract labour”
and is the agency a “contractor” under the
Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition)
Act, 1970?
options_english:
Yes, because they are physically executing
technical setup and maintenance work inside
the school premises.

Yes, because the computer supplier agency
is producing a given tangible result for the
establishment.

No, because IT technicians and hardware
engineers are legally barred from being
considered workmen.

No, because the transaction is a mere supply
of goods and under the 20-worker threshold.
questions.explanation_english:
No, because the transaction is a mere supply
of goods and under the 20-worker threshold.
Section 2(1)(c) excludes persons who merely
supply goods or articles of manufacture to an
establishment from being classified as contractors.
Furthermore, deploying only two technicians
falls far below the statutory workforce threshold
of twenty workers, excluding the transaction and
personnel entirely from the purview of the Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: स्रोत के अनुसार, केवल वस्तुओं की आपूर्ति और सीमा से कम तैनाती के इस उदाहरण में अधिनियम लागू नहीं माना गया है।
key_facts:
Correct option (English): No, because the transaction is a mere supply
of goods and under the 20-worker threshold.

The

questions.question_english:
The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition)
Act, 1970 balances the interests of the employer
and the contract labour by focusing heavily on:
options_english: Enhancing the profit margin of the contractor

Improving the working conditions and
welfare of the contract labour

Mandating equal pay for all ranks of regular

Transferring the administrative burden

questions.explanation_english:

welfare of the contract labour
The principal focus of the Contract Labour
(Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 is to
safeguard contract workers by improving their
working conditions, guaranteeing timely wage
payments, and mandating essential welfare
facilities such as canteens, rest rooms, and
first-aid kits. This statutory framework ensures
balanced operational practices between principal
employers and contractors while eliminating
labor exploitation.
